subject: Re: MEETING OF THE COUNCIL - 22 OCTOBER AT 7.00PM
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text:
Dear Requester,

I would advise you that the agenda published on the Council's website 
and on our noticeboards specifies that this will be a remote meeting and 
that members of the public can attend and ask me to provide a Zoom link 
to attend. I can confirm that you will be given a reasonable opportunity 
to ask questions and make comments on any item of business specified to 
be transacted that is on the published agenda.

Kind regards,

---
Paul R. Egan BA, Chartered MCIPD, CiLCA, F. Inst. LM, FIPSM

Clerk to Llandough Community Council,

[address removed]

Vale of Glamorgan [postcode redacted]

Telephone [phone redacted]

Website www.llandough-cc.co.uk [1]

When you contact us

The information you provide (personal information such as name, address,
email address, phone number, organisation) will be processed and stored
to enable us to contact you and respond to your correspondence, provide
information and/or access our facilities and services.

Your personal information will be not shared or provided to any other 
third party. Your information may however be published in the public 
domain if you require the Council to discuss the matter raised.

For further information please see our full privacy notice on our 
website www.llandough-cc.co.uk [1]

The Council's mission statement is 'Serving our community, preserving 
our identity' The Council will always strive to:

  ·  Be open and accessible in all our decision making

· Be accountable in all our council activities

· Be responsive to the needs of the community

· Encourage community participation

On 2026-10-16 14:31, Requester wrote:

> Dear Mr Egan,
> 
> Thank you for your email confirming that the Council meeting on 22 
> October 2026 will now be held remotely only.
> 
> I object to the removal of the opportunity for residents to attend in 
> person and ask that the decision be reconsidered before the meeting.
> 
> I recognise that the Local Government and Elections (Wales) Act 2021 
> provides for remote meetings. My concern is not with councillors using 
> Zoom, but with the Council deciding that there will be no physical 
> public attendance, without explaining the reasons for that decision or 
> how the interests of local democratic participation have been 
> considered.
> 
> The Welsh Government's statutory guidance for community and town 
> councils recognises the importance of accessible meetings, public 
> participation and transparency. It also requires councils to have 
> regard to the guidance when exercising their relevant functions. The 
> Act's section 48, inserting paragraph 27A into Schedule 12 of the Local 
> Government Act 1972, requires the person presiding over an open 
> community council meeting to give members of the public in attendance a 
> reasonable opportunity to make representations about the business, 
> subject to the statutory exception.
> 
> I therefore ask the Council to:
> 
> 1. Reconsider whether a physical venue can be made available to 
> residents, even if all councillors participate remotely.
> 2. Confirm who made the decision to change the meeting to remote-only 
> and when it was made.
> 3. Identify the Council's published arrangements or policy governing 
> multi-location meetings and provide the relevant link or document.
> 4. Explain what consideration was given to residents' ability to 
> observe proceedings and participate effectively, and why a physical 
> public gallery was not provided.
> 5. Confirm that I will be given a reasonable opportunity to make 
> representations during the public participation item through the Zoom 
> meeting, in accordance with the applicable rules.
> 
> If the Council maintains its decision, please treat this email as a 
> request for the reasons and the relevant policy or resolution to be 
> recorded in the public record.
> 
> For clarity, my outstanding FOI internal review and my requests 
> concerning the retention of historic planning records are separate 
> matters. I do not ask the Council to determine either matter through 
> this objection.
> 
> I remain willing to participate constructively in the meeting. I ask 
> only that the Council take the concerns about public access seriously 
> and explain its decision.
> 
> Yours sincerely,
> 
> Requester
> 
>

> https://www.google.com/url?q=https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com&source=gmail&ust=1792226701788000&sa=E

> 
> First, my FOI to the Council (treated as such in your reply of 11 
> October) and the internal review request of 13 October remain open. I 
> am not asking the Council to pre-judge them at the meeting; I simply 
> ask that the review outcome or a firm date be communicated before or at 
> the meeting so that public participation is not conducted under a 
> section 12 refusal that has not been reviewed.
> 
> Second, I have placed preservation requests with The National Archives, 
> HM Land Registry, the MOD, South Wales Police and others concerning 
> 1988 records. If the Council holds any planning files, section 52/106 
> instruments or correspondence from 1988-1992 relating to planning refs 
> 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES, I would be grateful for confirmation
